112 sections: **99 built**, **12 partial**, **1 deferred**, **0 declined**, with 6 sub-items deliberately refused.

A section is *partial* when part of what it describes is built and part
is not; the note says which. A *refusal* is narrower and more
deliberate: something the document asks for that was considered and
declined, with the reason recorded. Those are collected at the end.

## What was refused, and why

**§8 — script.** A project file is shared, so a script field would make opening a schema equivalent to running its author's code. A restricted interpreter is a denylist, not a sandbox; the isolation that would work was measured and exists on one of three target platforms. Chapter 41 of the manual has the full reasoning, including what was tried.

**§59 — embedding-based detection.** It needs an embedding provider and no adapter offers one, so it would be a configuration option that never worked.

**§61 — detecting suspiciously realistic public identities.** Deciding whether a generated name belongs to a real person needs a list of real people, which is a thing this project should not build and should not ship. Section 61's other three detectors are decidable from the value itself and are built; this one is not, and pretending otherwise would be worse than declining it.

**§61 — claiming the output is privacy-preserving.** Section 61 says not to claim it without an actual privacy technique, and detection is not one. It catches leakage, which is a smaller and different thing, and the documentation says so.

**§67 — semantic quality scoring.** It requires a judge model, which would make the benchmark depend on the kind of thing it is assessing. What is measurable is measured and named honestly instead.

**§69 — GPU generation time.** It cannot be estimated without the provider saying how long a step takes on its hardware, and no adapter reports that. A number invented here would be a guess wearing a unit.

## What is deferred

In the design, not built, and not refused - which means it is a schedule rather than a decision.

- **§33** PostgreSQL
- **§33** MySQL/MariaDB
